newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ZENGA TIRED OF INSULTS IN ITALY - NEWSPAPERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ZENGA TIRED OF INSULTS IN ITALY - NEWSPAPERS.

text.p: Former Italy goalkeeper Walter Zenga said he was leaving for a new career in the United States because he was fed up with being insulted at home, newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Zenga, who announced on Monday that he was leaving second division club Padova for a two-year contract with the New England Revolution in Boston, said his decision to go was influenced by the attitude of fans in Italy.
"In truth I was fed up with being insulted," the 36-year-old, dubbed "Spider Man" in Italy, told Italian newspapers.
"The Americans may have a lot of defects but at least they don't go to their stadiums to shout against you," Zenga said.
Zenga, who played 58 times for Italy, said he was tired of being spat at, hearing insults against his wife and children and constant chants of "Argentina, Argentina".
Zenga was in goal when Argentina beat Italy on penalties in the 1990 World Cup semifinal played in Naples.
"Let's be straight. Once they said the stress and tension justified the wages," La Repubblica quoted him as saying.
"Now in Germany and England they pay better with the difference that after the match you go to the pub and have a few drinks with your opponents.
"I suppose now they will say the dinosaur has spoken. But here they throw bathroom taps on the pitch. I'm going to America and, who knows, maybe I'll stay there."
Last month fans at the Reggiana-Parma serie A match threw metal objects, including a tap, at the Parma goal.
